cluster_summary: Multiple vulnerabilities arise from deserialization or class loading mechanisms that fail to properly validate the types being instantiated. Attackers can supply arbitrary class names, either through polymorphic deserialization, reflection, or metadata fields, leading to instantiation of dangerous gadgets or unauthorized objects. The predominant pattern involves an incomplete blocklist that misses known dangerous classes, while other cases involve no validation at all or flawed filtering logic.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Implement an allowlist of permitted classes or restrict class loading to a safe subset..
